name: Header
description: Groups the brand, navigation, dropdowns, search, actions and navigation trigger in a top bar.

children.description: Header content: Header.Brand, Header.Nav, Header.Search, Header.Actions, Header.Trigger, Header.SkipLink

position.description: `sticky` keeps the bar at the top of its scroll container

elevatedOnScroll.description: Draw the bottom hairline once the page scrolls (no shadow). Object form accepts { threshold?: number }, default 16.

when: Top-level navigation for an app or site
Anywhere brand, nav and actions share one row
whenNot: Section headings inside a page (use Main.Header)
guidelines: Header.Actions sits on the trailing edge on its own; there is no spacer part
Omit Header.Brand when the sidebar already shows the product name
Header.NavMenu groups related pages behind one trigger; mark the group active when the current page is inside it
Inside AppShell or Sidebar.Provider, Header.Trigger opens the sidebar's mobile panel and shows only while the rail is out of view
Without a sidebar, open a Drawer of Sidebar.Item rows from Header.Trigger for small screens
Pass render={<RouterLink />} to Brand or NavItem for router links
Header.SkipLink should be the first child
accessibility: Header.Nav is a labelled navigation landmark (default "Main navigation")
The current item carries aria-current="page"; a disabled item is aria-disabled and leaves the tab order
Header.Trigger has an accessible label and aria-expanded; inside a sidebar it also sets aria-controls
Header.NavMenu is a Base UI menu: click or Enter opens it, arrow keys move, Escape closes
Nav items keep a 32px track and a hit area that grows to 44px under a coarse pointer

examples.name: App Bar
examples.description: Brand, nav with the current page marked, and one action.
examples.code:
import { Button } from '@/components/Button';
import { Header } from '@/components/Header';

<Header>
  <Header.SkipLink />
  <Header.Brand href="/">Fragments</Header.Brand>
  <Header.Nav>
    <Header.NavItem href="/overview" active>Overview</Header.NavItem>
    <Header.NavItem href="/findings">Findings</Header.NavItem>
    <Header.NavItem href="/settings">Settings</Header.NavItem>
  </Header.Nav>
  <Header.Actions>
    <Button variant="soft">Sign in</Button>
  </Header.Actions>
</Header>

examples.name: With Dropdown Nav
examples.description: Header.NavMenu groups related pages behind one trigger.
examples.code:
import { Header } from '@/components/Header';

<Header>
  <Header.Brand href="/">Fragments</Header.Brand>
  <Header.Nav>
    <Header.NavItem href="/overview">Overview</Header.NavItem>
    <Header.NavMenu label="Workspace" active>
      <Header.NavMenuItem href="/findings">Findings</Header.NavMenuItem>
      <Header.NavMenuItem href="/settings" active>Settings</Header.NavMenuItem>
    </Header.NavMenu>
  </Header.Nav>
</Header>

examples.name: With Search
examples.description: Search between brand and actions; the Input owns its fill.
examples.code:
import { Button } from '@/components/Button';
import { Header } from '@/components/Header';
import { Input } from '@/components/Input';

<Header>
  <Header.Brand href="/">Fragments</Header.Brand>
  <Header.Search>
    <Input placeholder="Search…" aria-label="Search" />
  </Header.Search>
  <Header.Actions>
    <Button>New check</Button>
  </Header.Actions>
</Header>

examples.name: Sticky Marketing Bar
examples.description: Sticks to the top and draws the hairline once the page scrolls.
examples.code:
import { Button } from '@/components/Button';
import { Header } from '@/components/Header';

<Header position="sticky" elevatedOnScroll>
  <Header.SkipLink />
  <Header.Brand render={<a href="/" />}>Fragments</Header.Brand>
  <Header.Nav>
    <Header.NavItem href="/docs">Docs</Header.NavItem>
    <Header.NavItem href="/pricing">Pricing</Header.NavItem>
  </Header.Nav>
  <Header.Actions>
    <Button>Start trial</Button>
  </Header.Actions>
</Header>

examples.name: Mobile Navigation
examples.description: Without a sidebar, the trigger opens a Drawer of Sidebar.Item rows.
examples.code:
import { Drawer } from '@/components/Drawer';
import { Header } from '@/components/Header';
import { Sidebar } from '@/components/Sidebar';

const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);

<>
  <Header>
    <Header.Trigger aria-expanded={open} onClick={() => setOpen(true)} />
    <Header.Brand href="/">Fragments</Header.Brand>
  </Header>
  <Drawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
    <Drawer.Content side="start">
      <Drawer.Header><Drawer.Title>Navigation</Drawer.Title></Drawer.Header>
      <Drawer.Body>
        <Sidebar.Nav>
          <Sidebar.Section>
            <Sidebar.Item href="/overview" active>Overview</Sidebar.Item>
            <Sidebar.Item href="/findings">Findings</Sidebar.Item>
          </Sidebar.Section>
        </Sidebar.Nav>
      </Drawer.Body>
    </Drawer.Content>
  </Drawer>
</>

relations.note: Header.Trigger opens the sidebar's mobile panel and brings back a hidden rail
Without a sidebar, Header.Trigger opens a Drawer of Sidebar.Item rows
The colour-mode control (a ToggleGroup wired to useTheme) commonly sits in Header.Actions

propsSummary: elevatedOnScroll: boolean|{ threshold?: number } - the scroll hairline
Header.Brand and Header.NavItem take render for router links
Header.NavMenu label|active|disabled - a Base UI menu group
